title: The Trees: How Super Very More Sculpted the Organic Universe
content:
## _Motion graphics studio_[ _Super Very More_](https://superverymore.tv/the-trees) _shares the creative journey behind "The Trees," a cinematic project that reinterprets organic natural forms through the lens of Marvelous Designer’s fluid cloth simulation._

# **Could you please introduce your team and the artists who participated in this project?**

Hello, we are Super Very More, a motion graphics studio based in South Korea. The team members for this project include our lead artist, Chanwoo Kim, along with artists Haena Jang and Minkyung Park. The project was directed by Youngmin Kim.

# **Let’s talk about ‘The Trees,’ the project you created using Marvelous Designer. Where did you find inspiration for the concept, and what was the visual style you aimed to achieve?**

<https://superverymore.tv/the-trees>

When we first began planning this project, we spent a lot of time reflecting on what kind of insights we could offer other users, especially since we don't consider ourselves "specialists" in Marvelous Designer. Since there are already so many talented artists showcasing incredible performance with traditional MD workflows, we decided to focus on what we do best.

We explored a wide range of creative approaches to integrating Marvelous Designer into motion graphics—from standard techniques and simple applications to intentionally complex and experimental use cases.

![4456be98c8c9449ea5a6916d1e2e6b72](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/4456be98c8c9449ea5a6916d1e2e6b7213e8b8d0-a698-4d1f-9c5e-df0f04c780f0.png)As we brainstormed these various ways to utilize the software, we needed a strong metaphor to tie all our ideas together. That’s how we arrived at the concept of "Trees." Trees exist in countless forms across the world; sometimes they take on eerie, fantastical shapes that look as though they were intentionally designed by someone. We felt this perfectly aligned with the forms we wanted to express.

![92caa55dae1442e9a2f2b333e177e29b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/92caa55dae1442e9a2f2b333e177e29bThe%20Natural%20Tree%201.png)![eadc35f5146845d89743ce398cd002de](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/eadc35f5146845d89743ce398cd002deThe%20Transforming%20Tree%202.png)![f510a982b3eb45c89d8b9c9956b30a66](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/f510a982b3eb45c89d8b9c9956b30a66The%20Rythmic%20Tree%202.png)

Visually, we wanted each tree to feel highly detailed and grand in scale. Our goal was to create a cinematic piece with plenty of visual interest—a video that offers a sense of "paradoxical fun" by being both tranquil and spectacular at the same time. We believe that this essence is what defines motion graphics, and it’s exactly what we excel at.

![61ba146daa0546279963355796c06215](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/61ba146daa0546279963355796c06215trees%20final%20cut.png)

# **How did each of you use Marvelous Designer in this project? Also, if you discovered any "pro-tips" during the process, please share them with us!**

**Chanwoo** :

In my part of the project, I created an effect that took advantage of the "Sewing" property, where seam lines snap together instantly when the simulation starts. I felt this was a unique and playful way of expressing form that is only possible in Marvelous Designer.

Another standout strength is the ability for the user to intervene in real-time during a simulation. By using the "Pull" and "Push" functions, I could control the fabric intuitively as if I were physically shaking real cloth. This was incredibly useful for creating those one-of-a-kind, organic shapes.

![48738e7c39bd4ba8bb3affcf716b22ed](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/48738e7c39bd4ba8bb3affcf716b22edwork%20process%204.gif)![2bc02f3309ee4e0fb8636bc8a58bfb60](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/2bc02f3309ee4e0fb8636bc8a58bfb60work%20process%206.gif)![4070ce2fc6eb42f98fd948bb79ed354d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/4070ce2fc6eb42f98fd948bb79ed354dThe%20Rythmic%20Tree%201.png)

**Haena** :

I focused on the "Elastic" feature. I first created a flower bud shape by gathering the edges of the fabric. Then, by gradually lowering the Elastic values, I allowed the bundled fabric to spread out naturally, creating a motion that looked like a flower blooming.

The software's ability to express realistic and detailed wrinkles is a huge advantage. In particular, even high-resolution polygon simulations—which can feel quite heavy in Cinema 4D—could be tested very lightly and quickly here, which significantly boosted my efficiency.

![3809196538c74bedb8c208ed9f65ea17](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/3809196538c74bedb8c208ed9f65ea17The%20Transforming%20Tree%203.png)![b7317cd1dc154c67bb06cfba8987f278](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/b7317cd1dc154c67bb06cfba8987f278ezgif-6959cd0d1504b236.gif)![c51d5f2d991d47959cf3850be694c036](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/c51d5f2d991d47959cf3850be694c036The%20Natural%20Tree%202.png)

**Minkyung** :

I utilized the various "Fabric" presets to create a "Morph" effect, where a rigid material like raw denim transforms into soft silk. By adjusting and keyframing values for Gravity, Air Damping, and Wind to match the characteristics of each material within the simulation environment, I was able to sophisticatedly express the changing textures and surroundings.

It was incredibly appealing to be able to use multiple simulation features in combination while still being able to record and edit the results easily. For those who want to achieve detailed simulation results quickly and efficiently, I highly recommend actively experimenting with Marvelous Designer’s wide range of options.

![1b146d82436b433db414a234f3a585c3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/1b146d82436b433db414a234f3a585c3work%20process%201.gif)![c71a8a072ca6433ba5fac96247d4a188](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/c71a8a072ca6433ba5fac96247d4a188The%20Transforming%20Tree%201.png)![06f14803bdec4eb1b3a187a07679c18b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/06f14803bdec4eb1b3a187a07679c18bwork%20process%205.gif)![f0f6b22806f347bdb9092f54743b5f25](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/f0f6b22806f347bdb9092f54743b5f25The%20Rythmic%20Tree%204.png)

# **Since Cinema 4D (C4D) is a main part of your pipeline, how was the compatibility and overall usability between Marvelous Designer and C4D?**

**Chanwoo** :

In terms of basic compatibility, the connection was seamless without any major issues. However, when reprocessing Alembic files in Cinema 4D, there is a step where you need to convert them to an 'Editable' state for more flexibility. I found that this process significantly increases the file size, which was a bit challenging to manage. I think it’s important to strategically choose your workflow depending on whether you'll use the file simply as a final simulation result or as an element for further modification.

**Haena** :

The workflow between the two programs felt very continuous and fluid, which made the overall process highly efficient. It saved a lot of time because I didn’t need to do much additional cleanup or reorganization within Cinema 4D. I was particularly satisfied with the fact that the UVs come over already unwrapped, allowing me to skip complex UV tasks. Also, being able to check high-fidelity previsualizations in Marvelous Designer made it much easier to increase the final quality later when applying lighting and textures in C4D.

![8a30531cf6ee4a9c96847585f3da8df1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/a2c1244120dc4571a4954c7739dcdb98/images/8a30531cf6ee4a9c96847585f3da8df1work%20process%202.gif)One observation, however, is that compared to C4D’s 'Soft Body' simulation, Marvelous Designer tends to feel relatively flexible even with thicker fabric materials. It would be even better if future updates allow for more freedom in expressing stiffer, weighted materials with fewer wrinkles.

**Minkyung** :

I found that a methodical process works best: instead of creating every source from scratch in Marvelous Designer, I pre-plan the motion paths and positions in Cinema 4D, import them into Marvelous Designer for the simulation, and then bring them back to C4D. Early in the project, I faced some trial and error by overlooking the fact that you can't set 'Transform' keyframes directly within Marvelous Designer. However, by repeating the process of moving between the two tools using FBX and Alembic files, I was able to achieve a much more flexible workflow.

One thing to be careful about is the difference in 'Unit' settings between the two programs. Also, I noticed that if you modify the 'Particle Distance' in Marvelous Designer after creating the result, the point structure changes from the original source used in C4D, which can break 'Morph' targets. If you keep these characteristics in mind, you can build a very efficient workflow. I believe that providing more of these useful tutorials will greatly help motion graphics designers utilize these tools in a more structured and planned way.

# **How do you envision expanding the role of Marvelous Designer in your upcoming workflows?**

**Chanwoo** :

Moving forward, I want to actively incorporate Marvelous Designer into projects that require abstract, non-traditional graphics. I’m particularly interested in creating surreal visuals where the line between fabric and liquid becomes blurred, as I believe this is a powerful way to communicate a brand’s identity to its audience. To me, the true charm of Marvelous Designer lies in the "accidental beauty" that emerges from its unpredictable, organic flow.

**Haena** :

It will remain my go-to tool whenever I need detailed, realistic attire or specific fabric textures. Beyond that, I plan to utilize Marvelous Designer for projects that require unique and complex simulations—the kind of motion that is difficult to achieve through standard keyframe animation alone—to further elevate the overall production quality.

**Minkyung** :

I’d like to dive deeper into using the software for non-standard natural elements. For instance, heavy simulations involving multiple layers of objects swaying in the wind—like smoke or flower petals—can be controlled both precisely and efficiently within Marvelous Designer. Building on its unrivaled ability to express fabric wrinkles, I intend to apply its core features to a wider variety of creative directions.

I was particularly impressed by the 'Air Damping' option during this project, and I’m looking forward to experimenting with it further to create deep, immersive visual expressions in future projects set in underwater environments.

[**_Behance_**](https://www.behance.net/superverymore)

[** _Instagram_**](https://www.instagram.com/superverymore?igsh=bDhqaWV4N3llbnlr)
content_description: Explore the creative journey of Super Very More as they redefine organic forms through their cinematic project "The Trees," utilizing Marvelous Designer's innovative cloth simulation techniques.

title: COSMOS LAC Brand Promotion - 3D Motion Graphic with Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/8c3a69dfbff145adb95ef7a435f95db8thumbnail.jpeg)_3D Motion Graphic Designer_[ _Youngpyo Hwang_](https://www.behance.net/hwangzeti) _specializes in capturing "extraordinary moments" through seamless visual storytelling. In his latest project, ‘_[ _COSMOS LAC_](https://www.behance.net/gallery/242160349/COSMOS-LAC-Brand-Promotion) _,’ Hwang explores the message of "Wake Up Your Individuality" through the lens of street culture. By integrating Marvelous Designer into his first major 3D workflow, he brings this vision to life with dynamic cloth simulations and diverse streetwear silhouettes._

* * *

#   
_[_**_Artist Introduction]_**_  
_**Could you start with a brief introduction of yourself?**

![1a27b5976ead4e82aabf73d906e6fb1a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/1a27b5976ead4e82aabf73d906e6fb1aCharacter_01-ezgif.com-gif-to-webp-converter.webp)  
Hello, I am Youngpyo Hwang, a 3D Motion Graphic Designer. I started my journey in motion graphics because I was fascinated by the process of translating stories and emotions into visual language. As an artist, I strive to create "extraordinary moments" within a natural, seamless flow.

# **_[About the ‘COSMOS LAC’ Project]_**  
**The ‘COSMOS LAC’ project is very impressive. Could you tell us more about it?**

![e70d5747e66949508e05280f9d3a2211](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/e70d5747e66949508e05280f9d3a2211Character_02-ezgif.com-gif-to-webp-converter.webp)  
The ‘COSMOS LAC’ project is a milestone work I completed at the ‘[105class](https://shin105.com/)’ 3D Motion Graphics Academy. It marks my first transition into 3D after gaining experience in 2D motion graphics. This project was a meaningful exploration of new workflows and visual possibilities, as I applied the design sensibilities I developed in 2D to the world of 3D.

The core message driving this promotional video is **"Wake Up Your Individuality."** Using COSMOS LAC products as a medium, I wanted to encourage viewers to discover and express their own unique personality and style rather than simply following others.

  * **Main Keywords:** "Peeling off" and "Revealing."

  * **Concept:** The concept centers on the idea that as the outer layers (conventional colors) peel away, one’s inherent individuality is revealed.

  * **Visual Inspiration:** I drew inspiration from the free-spirited and intuitive expression of graffiti culture using lacquer sprays.

  * **Symbolism:** By featuring a character on a skateboard—a symbol of subculture—I aimed to convey the message of prioritizing self-expression over the judgment of others throughout the entire piece.




# **_[Getting Started with Marvelous Designer]_**  
**How did you first encounter Marvelous Designer, and what was your experience like when you started? Specifically, was there a reason you decided to use it for this project?**

![54dc33b1ca5a4158bfa67c97ee3056a5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/54dc33b1ca5a4158bfa67c97ee3056a5%E1%84%86%E1%85%A1%E1%84%87%E1%85%B3%E1%86%AF%E1%84%85%E1%85%A5%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3_02.png)  
For this project, I wanted the costumes to simulate as naturally as possible in response to the character's dynamic movements. I decided to use Marvelous Designer because I believe it is the most effective tool for achieving that level of realistic expression.

I first came across Marvelous Designer while studying 3D motion graphics. While looking for references, I noticed that most works featuring impressive cloth simulations were created using Marvelous Designer. Seeing the quality of those results left a strong impression on me and inspired me to eventually incorporate it into my own creative workflow.

# **_[Character Outfit Design & Using Marvelous Designer]_**  
The character in your project showcases individuality by wearing six different outfits. What were your primary considerations when creating these outfits using Marvelous Designer?

Before diving into the production process, I’d like to explain why the character wears six distinct outfits. The COSMOS LAC lacquer spray line consists of six main color categories, and I designed six different styles to match each one. This was a visual device intended to demonstrate how a diverse range of personalities and styles can branch out from a single brand.

In the outfit creation process, my main focus was on the "fit." Since the overall mood of the project is hip and street-oriented, I designed the outfits with an overfit silhouette to naturally reflect the character’s individuality. To maintain visual consistency with street culture, I selected iconic items such as hoodies, jeans, workwear, sweat setups, and varsity jackets.

# **_[Animation Workflow]_**  
**The natural simulation of the clothing combined with the character’s dynamic motion is impressive. Could you walk us through your step-by-step animation workflow?**

![71d04bf941754573a66c8ca0573a7947](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/71d04bf941754573a66c8ca0573a7947ezgif.com-video-to-webp-converter.webp)

The process began with the character planning stage. To align with the hip mood of the video, I designed the character to resemble a black mannequin. I chose black as the base because it is a foundational color that harmonizes with any palette, allowing the various costumes and colors to stand out effectively.

Next, I moved into the animation phase. Since the video features many dynamic movements, I paid close attention to ensuring the character's motions and silhouettes looked natural. Once the animation was set, I exported the character as an Alembic file from Cinema 4D and brought it into Marvelous Designer for the cloth simulation.

After the simulation, I exported the clothing as an Alembic file and converted it to OBJ for custom texturing in Substance 3D Painter. Finally, I brought the textures back into Cinema 4D for lighting, final refinements, and rendering.

# **_[Experience with Marvelous Designer]_**  
**What was the most impressive feature or experience you had while using Marvelous Designer?**

![4ef4f2b28b604a7f848fe4caa3ef744e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/4ef4f2b28b604a7f848fe4caa3ef744e%E1%84%86%E1%85%A1%E1%84%87%E1%85%B3%E1%86%AF%E1%84%85%E1%85%A5%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3_04.png)![11964b3f7237466596a83d739526140b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202602/d7de754b248542028e756aafe762c722/images/11964b3f7237466596a83d739526140b%E1%84%86%E1%85%A1%E1%84%87%E1%85%B3%E1%86%AF%E1%84%85%E1%85%A5%E1%84%89%E1%85%B3_03.png)  
The most impressive aspect was the highly detailed cloth simulation. I had to adjust the length and width of the garments multiple times to achieve the specific "fit" I envisioned, and the flexibility to modify clothing on the fly was a standout feature.

Since the project features many dynamic scenes, the natural movement of the fabric and the realistic representation of different physical properties were crucial. To achieve this, I actively used the texture and physical property settings within Marvelous Designer to fine-tune the unique feel of each fabric. Furthermore, in segments with intense character movement, I used the **Tack** tool to pin specific parts of the garment. This prevented excessive distortion and ensured the simulation remained seamless and natural.

# **_[Experience with Marvelous Designer]_**  
**What did you find easiest to adapt to when first starting with Marvelous Designer, and were there any aspects that surprised you?**

The easiest part to adapt to was how intuitive and straightforward the process of adjusting the character's fit was. I also found it very impressive that I could slow down the frame rate of the imported character animation within Marvelous Designer to verify the simulation. This feature allowed me to inspect and adjust intricate movements in detail, which was a huge help in achieving natural-looking simulations even during highly dynamic motions.

On the other hand, something that surprised me was the viewport navigation. Since I primarily use Cinema 4D, the way you manipulate and view objects from various angles in the viewport felt somewhat different from what I was accustomed to in C4D.

# **_[Future Plans]_**  
**If you are planning future projects using Marvelous Designer, in what direction would you like to expand your work?**

While this project focused on objects with realistic proportions, I want to challenge myself with stylized characters in my next work. As I am a fan of rough-textured toon-rendering styles, I am interested in creating a new visual mood by combining the realistic simulations of Marvelous Designer with surreal, non-photorealistic textures.

I was also deeply inspired by a talk given by [**Superverymore**](https://superverymore.tv/the-trees) at the [_Motion Plus Design Seoul_](https://motion-plus-design.com/) conference, where they used Marvelous Designer to simulate objects like flowers and trees rather than just clothing. Taking inspiration from that, I plan to expand my use of Marvelous Designer beyond garments to various other objects, broadening the scope of my visual expression.
content_description: Discover the artistry of Youngpyo Hwang, a 3D Motion Graphic Designer who brings individuality to life through dynamic storytelling and innovative cloth simulations in his latest project, 'COSMOS LAC.'

title: Marvelous Designer’s YouTube Community Expands to Vietnam
content:
![5eb12f41db7c491882b036ae0ef39acf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202601/6904063703fe43f7b111a50060fd629e/images/5eb12f41db7c491882b036ae0ef39acfMD%20VN%20YT%20English%2BViet%20Promo.png)

One year ago, we opened our office in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Since then, our presence across Southeast Asia has continued to grow, alongside our local team and partnerships. As part of our commitment to the region, we’re excited to launch a new YouTube channel dedicated to our Vietnamese Marvelous Designer community.  
  
The channel will feature Marvelous Designer news, updates, and tutorials translated and dubbed in Vietnamese. It will also include original content, including features on traditional Vietnamese garments.  
  
We’re continuing to invest in Southeast Asia, and this time Vietnam in particular, by supporting local creators and building resources that are accessible, relevant, and long-term. This new channel is one more way we’re extending that work alongside Marvelous Designer users in the region.  
  
Subscribe to Marvelous Designer Vietnam: [HERE](https://www.youtube.com/@MarvelousDesignerVi%E1%BB%87tNam)
content_description: Discover our new YouTube channel dedicated to the Vietnamese Marvelous Designer community, featuring localized news, tutorials, and original content that celebrates traditional Vietnamese garments while fostering local creativity.
